skill.name: dependency-updater
skill.description: Smart dependency update checker with changelog summaries and breaking change detection.
skill.summary: Smart dependency update checker with changelog summaries and breaking change detection.
skill.author: CuriousLearner

security_audit.summary: The external command findings are false positives from markdown code fences and example skill invocations. The hardcoded URL is a documentation link in an example report, not evidence of network exfiltration or hidden execution.

finding_verdicts.reason: Lines 70-76 are a markdown code fence containing example @dependency-updater invocations. There is no executable script, shell interpolation, or user-controlled command execution.
The static hit is the closing backtick fence for usage examples, followed by prose update strategy guidance. It does not define or execute shell commands.
Lines 89-116 are a markdown example of the report format. The block contains sample dependency findings, not Ruby backticks or executable command logic.
The URL is a public React migration guide shown inside a sample report. It is documentation evidence, not code that performs a network request.

content.value_statement: Dependency updates can hide breaking changes and security urgency. This skill reviews project manifests, summarizes update risk, and recommends an order for safe upgrades.
actual_capabilities: Reviews dependency manifests for JavaScript, Python, Go, Rust, and Java projects.
Classifies updates as patch, minor, or major based on version changes.
Summarizes changelogs, release notes, breaking changes, and security fixes when sources are available.
Prioritizes updates by critical, high, medium, or low urgency.
Produces a dependency update report with risks and a recommended update order.
limitations: Requires project files or dependency manifests to be available in the session.
Changelog and vulnerability accuracy depends on accessible package and advisory sources.
Does not replace running tests after dependency changes.
Does not automatically update lockfiles unless the user asks and tools permit it.

use_cases.title: Plan a Safe Upgrade Sprint
use_cases.description: Review outdated dependencies and sequence changes by risk, urgency, and testing needs.

use_cases.title: Triage Security Updates
use_cases.description: Identify vulnerable or deprecated packages and decide which updates need immediate attention.

use_cases.title: Prepare Release Maintenance
use_cases.description: Summarize dependency changes before a release branch receives package updates.

prompt_templates.title: Check Project Dependencies
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of available manifest files.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this project for outdated dependencies. Summarize patch, minor, and major updates with a recommended order.

prompt_templates.title: Focus on Security Updates
prompt_templates.prompt: Check dependencies for known vulnerabilities, security advisories, and deprecated packages. Prioritize critical and high-risk updates first.

prompt_templates.title: Assess Major Version Changes
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze major dependency updates in this repository. Summarize breaking changes, migration notes, and required compatibility checks.

prompt_templates.title: Build an Upgrade Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced maintenance planning across package ecosystems.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a dependency upgrade plan across available manifests. Include risk levels, changelog notes, test focus areas, and rollout order.

output_examples.input: Review my package manifest before a maintenance release.
output: Critical updates: one web framework update fixes a security advisory.
High priority: one major UI library update needs migration review.
Recommended order: security fix, test suite, major update branch, remaining minor updates.
Major updates require compatibility checks for runtime version, peer dependencies, and build tools.
Deprecated packages should be replaced before routine minor updates.
Low-risk patch updates can wait until the planned maintenance window.

best_practices: Review changelogs before applying major or security-sensitive updates.
Update dependencies in small groups and run the full test suite after each group.
Use a separate branch and keep lockfiles aligned with manifest changes.
anti_patterns: Updating every dependency at once without reading release notes.
Ignoring peer dependency warnings after major framework updates.
Shipping dependency changes without staging or CI verification.

faq.question: Which package ecosystems does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers npm, Yarn, pnpm, Python, Go, Rust, Maven, and Gradle manifests when files are available.

faq.question: Can it detect security vulnerabilities?
faq.answer: It can identify known vulnerabilities and advisories when package data and advisory sources are available.

faq.question: Does it update files automatically?
faq.answer: The skill focuses on analysis and planning. File changes require a separate user request and suitable tool access.

faq.question: How does it handle breaking changes?
faq.answer: It checks major updates, changelogs, release notes, and migration guidance for compatibility risks.

faq.question: Is it useful with Dependabot or Renovate?
faq.answer: Yes. It can help review proposed updates and explain priority, risk, and testing needs.

faq.question: Can it replace project testing?
faq.answer: No. It helps plan updates, but tests and staging checks remain required before release.
